question: Does a photon-sector term improve same-source radial-velocity and proper-motion data after fitting a shared Milky Way rotation curve directly to the measured channel velocities?
motivation: The earlier source-by-source circular-speed inversion divides by geometric projections and produced a strong radial diagnostic that may be a projection artifact. This stage fits the measured velocities without division.

new_physics_interpretation.observable_meaning: A nonzero DeltaTheta_gamma is an effective geometric-optics signature, not yet a fundamental derivation of B_m dynamics.
new_physics_interpretation.open_branch: An anisotropic or time-dependent optical metric could affect annual parallax and secular proper motion differently; catalog-level astrometry cannot close that branch.
new_physics_interpretation.non_identifiability: A photon term that changes both channels by exactly the same circular-speed amount is algebraically absorbed into Theta(R) and cannot be identified with this test.

ordinary_nuisance_model.reason: Fitting x and y absorbs uncertainty in the adopted Solar motion instead of attributing it to photon physics; z is effectively unconstrained by this thin-disk sample and has negligible leverage.

requirements: lower held-out weighted RMS than the null with the same rotation-curve order
complete-source bootstrap 95 percent upper limit reaches 30 km/s
amplitude sign and scale remain stable for rotation-curve orders 0 through 3

claim_boundary: The radial-log model was motivated by the prior diagnostic and is exploratory, not a pristine confirmatory test.
The model assumes a photon anomaly that projects like circular motion; other directional tensors require separately frozen predictions.
The catalog is a Milky Way maser sample and does not by itself establish extragalactic rotation or cluster lensing behavior.
New physics remains admissible only if it produces additional falsifiable observables and passes stability, causality, polarization, frequency, and Solar-System tests.
